# __PROJECT_NAME__

> An Avalanche cross-chain dapp scaffolded with AvaKit. Send a message between two Avalanche L1s using Interchain Messaging (ICM / Teleporter), against a one-command local devnet. Next.js + @avakit/react + shadcn/ui + Foundry + avalanche-cli.

## Project map

- [contracts/src/AvaKitMessenger.sol](contracts/src/AvaKitMessenger.sol): one contract that both sends and receives ICM messages (implements ITeleporterReceiver). Deployed per chain, then linked: each side registers the other as its trusted remote.
- [lib/messenger-artifact.ts](lib/messenger-artifact.ts): compiled ABI + bytecode (browser deploy, no Foundry at runtime).
- [scripts/devnet.sh](scripts/devnet.sh): one command — two local L1s with ICM + relayer.
- [icm.config.json](icm.config.json): the two chains (RPC URL + hex blockchain ID); written by `pnpm devnet`.
- [lib/devnet.ts](lib/devnet.ts): config → AvaKit chains + `blockchainIdOf()`.
- [lib/deployed-contract.ts](lib/deployed-contract.ts): `useDeployedContract(name, chain)` — remembers a deployed messenger per chain instance (chain id + RPC URL) and only uses it once `eth_getCode` confirms bytecode, so addresses from before a devnet reset are dropped.
- [components/demo.tsx](components/demo.tsx): the Devnet Studio — live chain cards (block + ICM status), deploy on both chains, send, watch it arrive. Setup is a copy-command panel (never runs shell).
- [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md): agent guide (ICM API, the blockchainID-vs-chainId gotcha, rules).

## Key facts

- `destinationBlockchainID` is a **bytes32 hex blockchain ID**, NOT the EVM chainId. Use `blockchainIdOf(chain)`.
- TeleporterMessenger canonical predeploy: `0x253b2784c75e510dD0fF1da844684a1aC0aa5fcf` — passed to the messenger's constructor (immutable), the UI reads it from `icm.config.json`.
- The receiver requires BOTH `msg.sender == TELEPORTER` AND `trustedRemote[sourceBlockchainID] == originSenderAddress` — deploy, then link both sides (`setTrustedRemote`, owner-only) before sending.
- A message is at most 256 bytes of UTF-8 (`MAX_MESSAGE_LENGTH`): `sendMessage` reverts with `AvaKitMessenger: message too long` above that. The UI enforces the same limit with its own constant (`MAX_MESSAGE_BYTES`, counted with `TextEncoder`) — it does not read the getter, which older deployments lack.
- Delivery gas is fixed at 350,000 (`REQUIRED_GAS_LIMIT`), enough to store the longest message. Raise it together with the size limit.
- A registered remote must be non-zero: a chain with no remote set is rejected, and `setTrustedRemote(blockchainID, address(0))` stops trusting a chain.

## Key APIs

- Send: `AvaKitMessenger.sendMessage(destinationBlockchainID, destinationAddress, text)` — `text` is at most 256 UTF-8 bytes (the contract rejects longer messages; the UI checks first). Delivery = the destination's `messagesReceived()` going up; the UI reports "not delivered" after 30 seconds.
- Link: `AvaKitMessenger.setTrustedRemote(sourceBlockchainID, remoteMessenger)` (owner-only, once per side; `address(0)` unlinks)
- Receive: `receiveTeleporterMessage(sourceBlockchainID, originSender, message)` (verifies the source, stores `lastMessage`)
- Deploy/read/write: `deployContract`, `getWalletClient`, `readContract`, `ensureChain` from `@avakit/core`
- Wallet: `<ConnectAvalanche />`, `useAvaChain().setChain` to switch between the two L1s

## Run it

```
pnpm devnet   # start 2 local L1s + ICM + relayer
pnpm dev      # http://localhost:3000 (or the port Next prints)
```
